title: RL Fundamentals: Agent, Environment, State, Action & Reward
interviewAnswer: Reinforcement learning is sequential decision-making by interaction. An agent observes a state, chooses an action using a policy, receives a reward and transitions to a new state. The objective is not immediate reward alone, but maximizing expected cumulative return over time.
why: RL appears in robotics, recommendation/control, autonomous systems and modern LLM post-training. Interviewers often test whether you distinguish supervised labels from rewards generated by interaction.
intuition: Supervised learning says “here is the right answer.” RL says “try an action, observe the consequence, and learn which behavior creates long-term reward.”
deepDive: The standard formalism is a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with states S, actions A, transition dynamics P, reward R and discount γ. A policy maps states to action distributions. Because an action can affect future states, RL must solve temporal credit assignment and balance exploration with exploitation.
math:
Return: G_t = Σ_{k=0}^∞ γ^k r_{t+k+1}.
Objective: J(π)=E_π[G_0].
workedExample: A warehouse robot can take a short risky route or a longer safe route. Reward design must capture task completion, collisions and time; optimizing only the next-step reward can create bad long-term behavior.
commonMistakes: Defining RL as “training with rewards” without explaining sequential interaction.
Assuming the reward for the current step is the entire optimization objective.
production: Real systems require careful reward design, safe exploration, offline evaluation and constraints because a misspecified reward can optimize the wrong behavior.
